headline: Highest risk is data leakage: dbt-core can reach a data warehouse while awesome-prompts is a prompt-content source with no isolation or provenance controls documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing/prompt repository, so its outputs can contain attacker-controlled text. dbt-core consumes external inputs for analytics workflows, and no provenance or isolation controls are documented in either profile. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is copied into dbt-core runbooks, macros, or model SQL without review, injection is possible.
IF dbt-core treats imported text as instructions rather than data, prompt hijacking becomes feasible.
mitigations: Review any copied prompt text before use.
Keep prompt repositories separate from dbt project files.
Use a manual approval step before executing generated SQL.
Strip instruction-like text from imported content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call warehouse APIs, while awesome-prompts is a public prompt-content source with no stated data handling. If warehouse outputs or sensitive snippets are pasted into prompt materials, leakage can occur through the pair’s workflow. The profiles do not show direct exfiltration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF warehouse data is copied into awesome-prompts-derived prompts or examples, sensitive data may be exposed.
IF dbt-core outputs are stored in shared docs or tickets alongside prompt content, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not paste warehouse rows into prompt libraries.
Redact sensitive fields before sharing examples.
Restrict access to dbt outputs used for prompt authoring.
Separate analytics workspaces from prompt repositories.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on exported warehouse samples.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is not runnable and has no write or network surfaces, while dbt-core has allowlisted egress and warehouse API access. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write authority, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because the profiles show asymmetry rather than collision.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same writable workspace, file-level conflicts could emerge.
IF dbt-core is configured to write artifacts into a directory also edited by prompt content, collisions may occur.
mitigations: Keep separate directories for prompt content and dbt projects.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files.
Use read-only mounts for prompt repositories.
Check for overlapping output paths before runs.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply persuasive but unverified text, and dbt-core can operationalize analytics outputs against a warehouse. If dbt-core consumes prompt-derived instructions or examples without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect transformations or reports. The pair lacks documented validation gates, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF dbt-core uses prompt-derived SQL or model guidance without review, incorrect logic can propagate.
IF downstream reports or jobs are triggered from unverified prompt content, cascading errors become likely.
mitigations: Require human review of generated SQL.
Validate outputs against known test cases.
Keep prompt examples out of production model code.
Add a checklist for source verification.
requires-engineering: implement automated lineage and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, which may include regulated or residency-bound data, while awesome-prompts is a public content repository with no compliance controls documented. If regulated warehouse data is moved into prompt materials or shared outputs, retention and residency mismatches can occur. Only agent_b is directly relevant to the data class, so agent_a is cited for its public-content role.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is exported into prompt repositories, retention and residency controls may be violated.
IF prompt content is shared across jurisdictions without review, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in prompt examples.
Review retention settings for exported dbt artifacts.
Limit sharing of analytics outputs to approved regions.
Document data-class handling for prompt content.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware export controls.
